extracted.intended_audience: mathematics researchers preparing and submitting manuscripts to the journal Geometry & Topology
extracted.subtask_short: submitting math research to Geometry & Topology
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting a research manuscript to the journal Geometry & Topology, covering ethical requirements, file formats, required metadata, and production/proof procedures. Intended to ensure submissions meet the journal's editorial and production standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to meet our ethical guidelines on intellectual property, plagiarism, contributorship, and disclosure of financial support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the full policies for authors (linked). Authors must follow policies on intellectual property, avoid plagiarism, correctly list contributorship, and disclose financial support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript acknowledges that the manuscript is original and is not, in whole or in part, published or under consideration for publication elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are required to attest that the manuscript will not be submitted elsewhere while under consideration for this journal. The submitted article must not be a revision of a rejected article previously submitted to this journal, unless the authors have been explicitly invited to resubmit by the editorial board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors of papers submitted to this journal may use AI tools for light editing, such as spell-checking and help with grammar, without acknowledgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any use of AI in aid of the arguments in a paper or the citations in a paper must be acknowledged. Papers largely created by AI may not be submitted to this journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of editor
rubrics_metrics.description: During submission, authors will be asked to suggest one or more suitable editors to initially handle their submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should choose the editor whose interests are closest to the subject of the paper, but who is not directly connected to one of the authors (e.g., as a former advisor/student, a close relative, a colleague at the same institution, or a close collaborator). Sometimes after submission the manuscript is reassigned to another editor for handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Articles in GT are usually in English, but articles written in other languages will be considered, provided a relevant editor is comfortable with the language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the article is not in English, two versions of the abstract must be included, one in the language of the article and one in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and file submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission requires uploading the paper in PDF format. If your submission is accepted you will then need to supply source files, preferably in a variety of TeX or LaTeX, or in other software such as Word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please follow our LaTeX instructions for authors. Please do not use the public class file gtpart.cls, which is out of date. Use whichever class file you prefer (article.cls, amsart.cls, etc.), and we will convert this in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief abstract of about 150 words or fewer must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It should be self-contained and not make any reference to the bibliography. If the article is not in English, two versions of the abstract must be included, one in the language of the article and one in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords and subject codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Keywords and at least one Mathematics Subject Classification code for the article are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author information
rubrics_metrics.description: For each coauthor, postal address and affiliation (if appropriate) are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each coauthor must provide a valid email address that belongs only to that person and is not shared with anyone. Changes in email address should be communicated promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: References completeness and citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographical references should be complete, including article titles and page ranges. All references in the bibliography should be cited in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of BibTeX is preferred but not required. Tags will be converted to the journal format. Authors attest that all documents listed in the bibliography have been read and absorbed by at least one author. Their relevance to the submission should be highlighted by a description explicit enough to orient the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures quality and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures must be of publication quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After acceptance, you will need to submit the original source files in vector graphics format for all diagrams in your manuscript; vector EPS or vector PDF files are the most useful. Bundle your figure files into a single archive (using zip, tar, rar or other format of your choice) and upload on the link you will be provided at acceptance time. For questions, write to graphics@msp.org. Each figure should be captioned and numbered so that it can float. Small figures can be kept in the text (e.g., "The curve looks like this:").

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints / arXiv policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If your paper has previously been deposited on arXiv, we will need its arXiv number at acceptance time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows the journal to deposit the DOI of the published version on the paper's arXiv page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs and production deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Page proofs will be made available to authors (or to the designated corresponding author) in PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to acknowledge the receipt of proofs or to return corrections within the requested deadline may cause publication to be postponed.
